summary: This proposed standard defines an RTCP Extended Report block that lets bursts and gaps of discarded packets be reported separately from burst and gap loss metrics, for use in a range of RTP applications.

plainLanguage.summary: Sometimes packets arrive too late and are thrown away. This adds a way for a call to report that separately from packets that never arrived.

questions: what is a burst gap discard metric
what is rtcp xr block type 35
difference between packet loss and packet discard in rtp
subtitle: A compact RTCP report that says how many packets a receiver threw away, and in what bursts, without needing loss reports alongside it.

tldr.problem: A real-time media receiver sometimes discards packets that arrive too early, too late or as duplicates. The earlier burst/gap discard report only works together with a burst/gap loss report, even when losses and discards do not happen at the same time.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8015 defines an RTCP Extended Report block (block type 35) that carries the discard burst statistics on its own: total discards, number of bursts, total burst duration and packets expected in bursts.
tldr.outcome: A sender can see how bursty the discards are and adapt, for example by changing the packetization interval or the bitrate. It is a Proposed Standard and nothing in the unit metadata says it has been replaced.

today: RFC 8015 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2016, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends the block of RFC 7003 into a stand-alone report.

sections.title: Why a Separate Discard Report
sections.content:
RFC 8015 defines a new RTCP Extended Report (XR) block. It reports the proportion of packets that the receiver's de-jitter buffer discarded in a burst. How many packets are discarded depends on the de-jitter buffer algorithm the endpoint uses, and the RFC does not try to report that algorithm.

The older block in RFC 7003 depends on the burst/gap loss metrics of RFC 6958, so an endpoint that sends one also has to send the other. That is useful when losses and discards are correlated. When they are not, an application may prefer a concise block that reports only discard bursts and gaps. The block in this RFC is complete by itself and adds the total number of packets discarded, the total burst duration and the total number of bursts, all of which are missing from RFC 7003.
sections.plainLanguage: Before, you had to hand in two forms at once: one for lost packets and one for thrown-away packets. Now you can hand in just the thrown-away form.

sections.title: Received, Lost, Discarded, Bursts and Gaps
sections.content:
Every packet is classified as exactly one of received (or OK), discarded or lost. A packet is lost if it fails to arrive within an implementation-specific time window. A packet that arrives in that window but is too early or too late to be played out, or is thrown away before playout because of duplication or redundancy, is discarded. A packet is not discarded if a higher-layer decoder drops it later, for example because of a decoding error.

The words burst and gap follow RFC 3611. A burst is a period when the discard rate is high enough to cause noticeable quality degradation, generally a discard rate over 5 percent. A gap is a period when discards are infrequent and quality is generally acceptable.
sections.plainLanguage: A packet either shows up on time, shows up but is useless, or never shows up. A burst is a rough patch where lots of packets get tossed, and a gap is a calm stretch.

sections.title: The Independent Burst/Gap Discard Metrics Block
sections.content:
The block is identified by block type BT=35 and has a fixed Block Length of 5. A receiver MUST discard a block with any other length. The I field says whether the numbers cover the most recent interval (I=10) or a cumulative period (I=11). These metrics cannot be sampled, so senders MUST NOT use I=00 or I=01, and a receiver MUST discard a block that carries them. The six reserved bits MUST be zero and are ignored by receivers.

The remaining fields are:

  • SSRC of Source: 32 bits, as in RFC 3611.
  • Threshold: 8 bits, equal to Gmin in RFC 3611, the number of successive packets that must be received before and after a discarded packet for it to count as part of a gap.
  • Sum of Burst Durations (ms): 24 bits, the total duration of discard bursts in the report period.
  • Packets Discarded in Bursts: 24 bits.
  • Number of Bursts: 16 bits.
  • Total Packets Expected in Bursts: 24 bits, the sum of received and lost packets during the bursts.
  • Discard Count: 32 bits, packets discarded over the whole period of the report.

For the two counters that can overflow, an over-range value is reported as 0xFFFFFE (burst duration) or 0xFFFE (number of bursts), and an unavailable measurement as 0xFFFFFF or 0xFFFF.
sections.plainLanguage: The block is a short form with boxes to fill in: how many packets were tossed, how many clumps there were, and how long the clumps lasted.

sections.title: Measuring and Using the Numbers
sections.content:
Measurements are made at the receiving end of the stream. The block relies on the Measurement Information Block of RFC 6776 to say what period the report spans. Senders MUST send the two in the same compound RTCP packet, and a receiver MUST discard this block if the measurement period did not arrive in the same compound packet.

Two derived values are suggested. The average discarded burst size is Packets Discarded in Bursts divided by Number of Bursts. The average burst duration is Sum of Burst Durations (ms) divided by Number of Bursts. The RFC says the variation in discards within a burst affects user experience, so a sending endpoint can change the packetization interval or vary the bitrate based on the report. The report can also be used for diagnostics.

The metrics suit RTP applications that have de-jitter buffers and do not use stream repair such as forward error correction or retransmission. For Voice-over-IP without repair, if voice activity detection is used, burst and gap duration are determined as if silence packets had been sent, so silence longer than Gmin packets ends a burst.
sections.plainLanguage: If a call hears that packets keep getting tossed in big clumps, it can send smaller or fewer pieces at a time to cope.

sections.title: SDP Signaling and IANA
sections.content:
XR blocks can be used without prior signaling. When signaling is wanted, this RFC adds a new value to the SDP rtcp-xr attribute from RFC 3611: ind-burst-gap-discard. The offer/answer rules for unilateral rtcp-xr parameters in RFC 3611 apply unchanged.

IANA assigns block type 35 to the Independent Burst/Gap Discard Metrics Block in the RTCP XR Block Type registry and registers the SDP parameter ind-burst-gap-discard.
sections.plainLanguage: Two phones can say ahead of time that they will swap this report, but they are also allowed to just start sending it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The block carries no per-packet statistics, so the confidentiality risk described in RFC 3611 does not apply. The RFC does note that the timing of a discard burst could reveal when another stream on the path was active. It calls this not a significant threat, because only the timing is leaked and not the cause.

Where it is a concern, implementations SHOULD apply encryption and authentication to the block, for example by using the AVPF profile with the Secure RTP profile (the combination called SAVPF, specified in RFC 5124). Beyond that, the RFC believes the block adds no new security considerations beyond those in RFC 3611.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone who sees the report might guess when another video was using the same road. That is not a big deal, and you can lock the report if you care.

fields.name: I
fields.desc: Interval (10) or cumulative (11); 00 and 01 are not allowed.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Set to zero by senders, ignored by receivers.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: The stream being reported on, as in RFC 3611.

fields.name: Total Packets Expected in Bursts
fields.desc: Received plus lost packets during bursts.

fields.name: Discard Count
fields.desc: Packets discarded over the whole report period.
